findings.title: parse() ignores a minus sign when the input has leading noise text
findings.property: a duration written with a minus sign parses as negative, even when preceded by noise text that parse otherwise tolerates
findings.property_test: negative sign applies with noise prefix
findings.actual: 3600000 (sign silently dropped, because only str.trimStart()[0] === '-' is checked)
findings.evidence: README advertises noisy input ('duration: 1h:20min' is parsed) and negatives ('-1hr 40mins' => -1*h - 40*m). The sign is detected only at the first character of the whole string (index.js line 56), so the two documented features do not combine: the number is parsed from the noisy string but its sign is lost, giving a result with the wrong sign and no error.

error.message:
Expected values to be strictly equal:
+ actual - expected

+ 3600000
- -3600000

review.title: Minus sign is only recognised at the start of the string, not after leading text
review.reason: The code deliberately treats a negative as a leading '-' on the whole string (index.js:56), and the tests only cover that form ('-1hr 40mins', ' -1hr 40mins', '  -1h'). The README promises tolerance of noise text, not a sign that is detected after it. Treating any '-' inside noise as a sign would misread hyphenated text such as 'foo-bar 1h', ranges like '5-10min' and 'a - b'. The report assumes a combination of features that is not promised, and a maintainer is unlikely to accept a fix.
